minutes.headline: Board advanced the Gilchrist Street land exchange to its next step despite resident objections.
minutes.summary: The board heard a parent's complaint about a child missing after school pickup, then long public comment on the Gilchrist Street land conveyance. It saw the new town website, a stormwater permit update, and acted on a fair entertainment license, a transit contract, warrant dates, and a Hickory Hills easement. It voted on the unique-acquisition determination and argued over meeting in accessible school buildings.

what_happened.line: The board voted that acquiring a portion of 171 Gilchrist is a unique acquisition under chapter 30B, so advertising would not benefit the town.
The board voted to sign a grant of easement to the Hickory Hills lake association for dam work.
Residents spoke at length against conveying the Gilchrist Street path and asked what was agreed in executive session.
The board acted on the Stillman fair entertainment license, the Mart contract and the special Town Meeting warrant dates; the minutes record no audible outcome for these.
The board took no motion on holding meetings in other school buildings, and tabled the Matson drainage easement to September 18.

why_it_matters: The unique-acquisition vote lets the town skip public advertising for the Gilchrist Street land exchange, so residents who care about the path have fewer formal steps at which to weigh in before it comes to a Town Meeting vote.
A radio repeater at the primary school was raised as a capital item, which would be a future cost on the town budget, mostly taxes, and bears on how buses and schools reach dispatch.
watch_next: September 18: the Matson drainage easement returns to the board.
A workshop next week, with the state earmark wish list to go on a future workshop list.
